{"author":{"is_bot":true,"login":"app/quuu824016"},"baseRefName":"feat/ci-scope-pr-triggers","body":"Adopts `k-kinzal/php-ai-toolkit` in `packages/sql-faker`.

PHPStan is clean at level max with the toolkit's rules, the unit suite is green on PHP 8.1
through 8.5, and the mutation gate passes on the changed lines.

## Worth a look

- The grammar reader was split into named collaborators: `Grammar/SourceCursor`,
  `Grammar/Derivation`, `Grammar/TerminationCost`, `Grammar/LexicalProfileWriter`, and the
  `LexicalCatalogShape` / `LexicalWitnessShape` pair that say what a compiled profile is.
- The Bison and PostgreSQL grammar readers gained collaborators of their own, so reading a
  directive, a preamble or a start symbol each has an owner.
- Refusals are `GrammarParseException` / `GenerationException` / `LexicalCatalogException`
  rather than `InvalidArgumentException`, so a caller can catch what this package refuses
  without catching everything.

## Stack

Nine stacked PRs, one per package. Merge bottom-up:

1. #281 `sql-faker`
2. #282 `sql-fixture`
3. #283 `ztd-query-core`
4. #284 `ztd-query-mysql`
5. #285 `ztd-query-postgres`
6. #286 `ztd-query-sqlite`
7. #287 `ztd-query-pdo-adapter`
8. #288 `ztd-query-mysqli-adapter`
9. #289 `drop-custom-rules` — deletes `packages/phpstan-custom-rules`

A PR lower in the stack also triggers the workflows of the packages downstream of it,
because their `paths` filters name the package it changes; those downstream workflows stay
red until their own PR lands. #289 sits on top of the whole stack and is the one that shows
every package green at once — it is currently green on all 109 checks.

## What the toolkit changed, in every package

- `phpstan.neon` — `k-kinzal/phpstan-custom-rules` replaced by the toolkit's
  `extension.neon` and `rules.neon` alongside `phpstan-strict-rules`, at `level: max`.
- `.php-cs-fixer.dist.php` — byte-identical to the toolkit's template.
- `phpunit.xml.dist` — the toolkit's strict configuration and `AiTestReporterExtension`.
- `infection.json5` — the toolkit's thresholds, `maxTimeouts: 0`, `timeoutsAsEscaped`.
- `.github/workflows/<package>.yml` — the shape the toolkit's GitHub Actions and Infection
  skills ask for: actions pinned to commit SHAs, `permissions: contents: read`, per-job
  `timeout-minutes`, every gate a named step, a parallel-runner job, and a mutation job
  that pre-generates coverage and scores a pull request on its changed lines against
  `--min-msi=85 --min-covered-msi=85`.

## What the rules asked for, and what that meant

The toolkit forbids private and non-override protected methods, wants a paired unit test
for every public method, forbids `mixed` in any internal or scope-restricted declaration,
forbids catching `Throwable`/`Exception`, and wants a `@throws` tag for every checked
exception that escapes. Satisfying that is a design change rather than an annotation pass:
each private method either became a collaborator with a name and a test or became part of
its type's stated contract, and each `mixed` either got a named `@phpstan-type` on a public
boundary or was validated where it entered.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>","messageHeadline":"style(sql-faker): expand one-line PHPDoc and apply the wider fixer set","oid":"8bfb6161b1d5789c881a5ff9dc843b839f030630"},{"authoredDate":"2026-08-24T10:15:57Z","authors":[{"email":"319849249+quuuai[bot]@users.noreply.github.com","id":"BOT_kgDOExCDIQ","login":"quuuai[bot]","name":"quuuai[bot]"},{"email":"noreply@anthropic.com","id":"MDQ6VXNlcjgxODQ3","login":"claude","name":"Claude Opus 5"}],"committedDate":"2026-08-24T10:15:57Z","messageBody":"…r errors

The generators and grammar parsers reported every failure as a
LogicException, and LexicalException extended one too. That put "this
grammar file declares no rules", "this rule cannot be realized" and "this
SQL did not round-trip" in the same family as a violated precondition —
failures a caller is told to fix rather than handle. sql-faker reads Bison
and Lemon grammars that ship with the servers it targets and tokenizes SQL
it was handed, so all three are runtime conditions.

LexicalException now extends RuntimeException, and two new types carry the
rest: GrammarParseException for source text that yields no rules, and
GenerationException for a grammar that cannot derive a statement. Both are
recoverable, so a caller generating from a grammar it did not author can
catch them without also swallowing its own bugs.

The wording moves onto the exceptions as named constructors. The same eight
messages were spelled out across the MySQL, PostgreSQL and SQLite
generators, twice with wording that had drifted apart: SQLite named the
empty rule where the others did not, and MySQL said "derivation plan" where
the others said "generation plan". Both now report the more useful form.

Precondition guards are untouched: GenerationPlan, Grammar and
RandomStringGenerator still raise InvalidArgumentException when a caller
passes an empty rule name or an empty catalog, because those are defects at
the call site.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>","messageHeadline":"refactor(sql-faker): make grammar failures recoverable, not programme…","oid":"2be765e243e249f606a6060c7652b782d5d6a98a"},{"authoredDate":"2026-08-24T10:28:47Z","authors":[{"email":"319849249+quuuai[bot]@users.noreply.github.com","id":"BOT_kgDOExCDIQ","login":"quuuai[bot]","name":"quuuai[bot]"},{"email":"noreply@anthropic.com","id":"MDQ6VXNlcjgxODQ3","login":"claude","name":"Claude Opus 5"}],"committedDate":"2026-08-24T10:28:47Z","messageBody":"The toolkit rejects four habits the suite had picked up, and each one hid a
test that could not fail for the reason it claimed to.

Twelve cases expected an InvalidArgumentException or a LogicException from a
precondition guard: an empty rule name, an empty lexeme catalog, a zero-part
hostname. Those are defects at the call site, so the test only asserted that
broken input breaks. They are deleted; the guards they poked at stay.

Fifteen more asserted a class implements an interface or extends an
exception, which the engine already guarantees and no change to the class
body can break. Deleted too, along with the three-line variant that checked
the same thing for all three dialect lexers. PgGrammar::load() and
SqliteGrammar::load() kept their tests but now assert the loaded grammar has
rules, which is what a caller actually depends on.

Seven read method signatures through Reflection to check default argument
values. The contract they were reaching for is that calling with no
arguments matches calling with those values, so they now assert exactly
that, against one re-seeded generator. Two interface tests that asked
Reflection whether an interface is an interface now exercise the contract:
every Symbol reports its own value, and every Bison declaration kind can be
carried by an AST.

Test methods named after constructors are renamed for the behaviour they
pin down, and the anonymous Faker stubs declare the exception they throw.

Three Reflection uses remain in the SQLite generator tests. They read the
private augmented grammar, and they go away when that augmentation becomes a
collaborator with an API of its own.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>","messageHeadline":"test(sql-faker): assert behaviour instead of shape","oid":"509ce33dd7c6b1fcf358c44dd874241cb0b38ee9"},{"authoredDate":"2026-08-24T11:51:57Z","authors":[{"email":"320539145+quuu143225[bot]@users.noreply.github.com","id":"BOT_kgDOExsKCQ","login":"quuu143225[bot]","name":"quuu143225[bot]"},{"email":"noreply@anthropic.com","id":"MDQ6VXNlcjgxODQ3","login":"claude","name":"Claude Opus 5"}],"committedDate":"2026-08-24T11:51:57Z","messageBody":"BisonLexer had twenty-four private methods, and they were private for one
reason: every one of them read and moved $this->pos. Six were cursor
primitives, sixteen were the states of the scan, and the rest were a
lookahead buffer the parser needs. None of them could be reached without
also owning the position, so the interesting rules — what closes a
brace-delimited action, what a prologue does when the file is truncated —
were only observable by feeding a whole grammar file to next().

The position now belongs to SourceCursor, which every state receives as an
argument instead of reaching into. That is what removes the private
modifier; moving the same bodies onto another class would only have replaced
one shared field with a longer parameter list.

Each state is a BisonScanner that declares the character it starts on and
returns the token it read: DirectiveScanner, ActionScanner, TypeTagScanner,
QuotedLiteralScanner, NumberScanner, IdentifierScanner, PunctuationScanner.
BisonScannerChain holds the order, so the lexer dispatches by lookup and no
scanner knows the others exist. BisonTokenStream carries the lookahead, which
keeps the lexer a forward scan that never re-reads a token.

Trivia is not a scanner. Whitespace and comments may sit between any two
lexemes, so modelling them as lexemes would mean every scanner having to
answer "nothing this time" and the lexer looping until one of them did not.
BisonTrivia skips them before dispatch, which is what lets scan() promise a
token rather than a token-or-null, and turns the old recursion through
token() into a single pass. It also owns the one place a slash is not a
comment: inside an action body a slash is division, so recognising a comment
and requiring one are separate operations.

BisonTokenType is renamed BisonLexeme: it names what was read, not a type.

Two failures change shape. Unreadable grammar source now raises
GrammarParseException rather than a bare RuntimeException, and peekN() below
one raises InvalidArgumentException, because asking for the zeroth token
ahead is a defect in the caller rather than in the grammar.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>","messageHeadline":"refactor(sql-faker): make the Bison lexer's states explicit","oid":"159b8bc4462c60861202f1bfd198cf82ddd297fc"},{"authoredDate":"2026-08-24T13:35:02Z","authors":[{"email":"320539145+quuu143225[bot]@users.noreply.github.com","id":"BOT_kgDOExsKCQ","login":"quuu143225[bot]","name":"quuu143225[bot]"},{"email":"noreply@anthropic.com","id":"MDQ6VXNlcjgxODQ3","login":"claude","name":"Claude Opus 5"}],"committedDate":"2026-08-24T13:35:02Z","messageBody":"BisonParser held twenty private methods and three responsibilities: the
order of a grammar file's sections, the argument shape of each of the eight
declaration kinds, and how a rule's alternatives are assembled. They were
private because each one advanced a shared token stream, so `%define` could
only be exercised by handing a whole grammar file to parse().

The eight declaration shapes are eight different grammars — `%expect` takes
a number, `%token` takes names with optional codes and aliases,
`%parse-param` takes a block of host code — so each becomes a
BisonDirectiveReader that answers for its own directive.
BisonDirectiveReaderChain holds the routing, and the reader for directives
this parser has no model for sits last, which is what keeps an unrecognised
directive from swallowing the declarations after it. Where a declaration
ends was decided in four places by one predicate; it is now
BisonDeclarationBoundary, so those four cannot drift apart.

The rules section splits the same way. BisonRuleReader finds the rules,
BisonAlternativeReader reads one rule's alternatives, and the alternative
being read is BisonAlternativeDraft rather than five local variables that
had to be reset at each of the three places an alternative can end — the
place a forgotten reset would have attached one alternative's action to the
next. BisonPreambleReader and BisonStartSymbol carry what is left.

Readers were written as peek-then-consume, and PHPStan reported the result:
having narrowed the peeked lexeme, it could not see that consuming a token
changes it, so four comparisons looked constant. The stream was missing the
operation the readers actually wanted, and nextIf() is it — take the next
token only if it is one of these kinds. Reading a type tag, a token code or
an alias is now one step that cannot look at one token and consume another,
and the coercion those readers repeated moves onto BisonToken as asString()
and asInt().

BisonSymbolType becomes BisonSymbolForm and BisonTokenInfo becomes
BisonTokenDefinition: one records how a symbol was written, the other is a
terminal a %token directive declares.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>","messageHeadline":"refactor(sql-faker): give the Bison parser one reader per thing it reads","oid":"36d2369128f2bd67376c234ed0b0607b88d575b6"},{"authoredDate":"2026-08-24T13:48:55Z","authors":[{"email":"320539145+quuu143225[bot]@users.noreply.github.com","id":"BOT_kgDOExsKCQ","login":"quuu143225[bot]","name":"quuu143225[bot]"},{"email":"noreply@anthropic.com","id":"MDQ6VXNlcjgxODQ3","login":"claude","name":"Claude Opus 5"}],"committedDate":"2026-08-24T13:48:55Z","messageBody":"LexicalCatalog was two things: the validated catalog its callers ask
questions of, and the reading that turns a decoded resource file into one.
The reading was three private methods and thirty-one throw sites, fourteen
of which raised the same sentence — so a catalog regenerated from a changed
upstream lexer failed with "Invalid upstream lexical catalog shape." and no
indication of which field had moved.

Reading is now LexicalCatalogShape, section by section, with
LexicalWitnessShape for the individual lexing examples and their two
spellings. The two agreement checks are LexicalCoverageCheck, which holds the
partition rule — every unit of the upstream lexer witnessed or excluded,
never both and never neither — and LexicalWitnessCheck, which holds the
rule that the catalog' two halves refer back to each other. LexicalCatalog
keeps only the questions.

The thirty-one messages become LexicalCatalogException, one named
constructor per way the file can be wrong, and the shape failures now name
the field: "Field: coverage.witnessed" rather than the same sentence again.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>","messageHeadline":"refactor(sql-faker): read the terminal catalog before trusting it","oid":"763a170656747a3c390fda32f6a19c24a1724fdc"},{"authoredDate":"2026-08-24T14:15:03Z","authors":[{"email":"320539145+quuu143225[bot]@users.noreply.github.com","id":"BOT_kgDOExsKCQ","login":"quuu143225[bot]","name":"quuu143225[bot]"},{"email":"noreply@anthropic.com","id":"MDQ6VXNlcjgxODQ3","login":"claude","name":"Claude Opus 5"}],"committedDate":"2026-08-24T14:15:03Z","messageBody":"… back

MySql\LexicalGrammar held two inverse operations. Realization turns a
terminal into SQL; tokenizing turns SQL back into terminals; the class did
both and compared the results, so eighteen private methods belonging to one
side or the other shared a class with no way to reach either alone. Testing
that a run of digits widens from NUM to LONG_NUM at the right magnitude
meant generating a statement that happened to contain one.

MySqlTokenizer now owns reading, MySqlTerminalRealizer owns writing, and
LexicalGrammar owns the round trip that makes the pair worth having. The
tokenizer's rules are separate methods in the order the server applies them,
so the one that depends on what came before it — a hostname is a hostname
because an `@` preceded it — says so in its signature.

Three things the dialects were repeating move to SqlFaker\Grammar.
LexicalProfileSource loads a profile and refuses one that names a different
server than the caller asked for. LexicalKeywordIndex inverts the profile's
terminal-to-spelling map. LexicalException gains a named constructor per way
realization and tokenizing can disagree, each taking the dialect name, so
three copies of the same eight messages become one.

The round-trip message was rendering both token sequences with
JSON_THROW_ON_ERROR. Those sequences come from arbitrary generated bytes, so
the message could fail on exactly the input it exists to report; it now
substitutes what JSON cannot encode.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>","messageHeadline":"refactor(sql-faker): separate writing MySQL lexemes from reading them…","oid":"fbdf9237737dc2f664a842d53d1d8a1803d87877"},{"authoredDate":"2026-08-24T23:53:38Z","authors":[{"email":"320539145+quuu143225[bot]@users.noreply.github.com","id":"BOT_kgDOExsKCQ","login":"quuu143225[bot]","name":"quuu143225[bot]"},{"email":"noreply@anthropic.com","id":"MDQ6VXNlcjgxODQ3","login":"claude","name":"Claude Opus 5"}],"committedDate":"2026-08-24T23:53:38Z","messageBody":"…ects

PostgreSql\LexicalGrammar and Sqlite\LexicalGrammar held the same conflation
MySQL's did: realization turns a terminal into SQL, tokenizing turns SQL back
into terminals, and both lived in one class with thirty-five private methods
between them. Neither half could be exercised without the other.

PgTokenizer and SqliteTokenizer own reading, PgTerminalRealizer and
SqliteTerminalRealizer own writing, and each LexicalGrammar owns the round
trip. PostgreSQL gains a third: the substitutions its parser frontend makes
by looking ahead were spelled out in three places — once when tokenizing,
once when normalizing a derivation, and once when realization had to find the
keyword a substituted token borrows its spelling from. PgLookahead states
that rule once, in the three directions those callers need it.

Both dialects now load their profile through LexicalProfileSource, index
their keywords with LexicalKeywordIndex, and raise LexicalException's named
constructors, so the file-loading, index-building and message-wording that
were written three times are written once.

The SQLite realizer's twenty-three operator terminals were arms of a match
that mapped each to its spelling; they are a table, and are one now. The
STRICT table option keeps a terminal of its own because SQLite spells it as
an ordinary identifier, and the reason is recorded where the constant is.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>","messageHeadline":"refactor(sql-faker): split writing from reading in the other two dial…","oid":"394c080dc8944ed4c6ec7ada76e755a6447b7657"},{"authoredDate":"2026-08-24T23:58:23Z","authors":[{"email":"320539145+quuu143225[bot]@users.noreply.github.com","id":"BOT_kgDOExsKCQ","login":"quuu143225[bot]","name":"quuu143225[bot]"},{"email":"noreply@anthropic.com","id":"MDQ6VXNlcjgxODQ3","login":"claude","name":"Claude Opus 5"}],"committedDate":"2026-08-24T23:58:23Z","messageBody":"…exercises

The plan factories were tested, but under names that described the grammar
being restricted rather than the method doing the restricting, so nothing

The lexical factories had no tests at all — twenty-six methods whose whole

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>","messageHeadline":"Say in the type what a plan refuses, and name the enum for what it holds","oid":"07d8941ce23cac60b5a578111095cd99fdf9a7b2"},{"authoredDate":"2026-08-25T01:09:35Z","authors":[{"email":"320539145+quuu143225[bot]@users.noreply.github.com","id":"BOT_kgDOExsKCQ","login":"quuu143225[bot]","name":"quuu143225[bot]"},{"email":"noreply@anthropic.com","id":"MDQ6VXNlcjgxODQ3","login":"claude","name":"Claude Opus 5"}],"committedDate":"2026-08-25T01:09:35Z","messageBody":"Each generator kept a step counter as a field and reached into it from a

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>","messageHeadline":"Pin the tables the mutation gate could still remove entries from","oid":"5203fe1eec970a4c99e3b2c5e5e10b204547a754"},{"authoredDate":"2026-08-26T05:13:42Z","authors":[{"email":"320962924+quuu824016[bot]@users.noreply.github.com","id":"BOT_kgDOEyGBbA","login":"quuu824016[bot]","name":"quuu824016[bot]"},{"email":"noreply@anthropic.com","id":"MDQ6VXNlcjgxODQ3","login":"claude","name":"Claude Opus 5"}],"committedDate":"2026-08-26T05:13:42Z","messageBody":"…tings

The toolkit split its rule registrations out of extension.neon into a new
rules.neon. Our phpstan.neon included only the former, so after the update not
one of the 39 toolkit rules was running. It also carried a local copy of the
exception policy, which overrode the one rules.neon now owns. Both are gone:
the configuration is the three baseline includes and level max, and analysis
paths move to the Composer script so the file stays only the toolkit contract.

PHPUnit gains the strictness the current template requires — sealed mock
objects, strict about tests that assert nothing, details on all issues,
unshortened arrays in failure output, indirect deprecations ignored rather
than all of them, and coverage that neither hides untouched files nor honours
ignore metadata. The redundant failOn* attributes go; failOnAllIssues covers
them and opts into issue types later releases add.

Infection moves to the toolkit policy of 80/80 on the whole tree, counts a
timed-out mutant as escaped, and writes a per-mutator report so the escapees
can be read rather than guessed at. Formatting stops walking build/, which is
where those reports now land.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>","messageHeadline":"Re-apply php-ai-toolkit at its current release, without the loose set…","oid":"87fcfb4fb75e98d3bb34614a3b12f6c2d024a467"},{"authoredDate":"2026-08-26T14:08:25Z","authors":[{"email":"320962924+quuu824016[bot]@users.noreply.github.com","id":"BOT_kgDOEyGBbA","login":"quuu824016[bot]","name":"quuu824016[bot]"}],"committedDate":"2026-08-26T14:08:25Z","messageBody":"The three attributes removed here arrived in PHPUnit 12. This package
supports PHP 8.1, where PHPUnit 10.5 resolves, refuses the configuration
outright, and turns that refusal into a warning — which failOnAllIssues
then makes a red build on three of the five versions CI covers.

Everything else the configuration asks for is understood by every line
from 10.5 up, so the rest stands.","messageHeadline":"Set only the strictness every supported PHP version can read","oid":"850391c96ee14d8b2f791205bf3d56439fced3cc"},{"authoredDate":"2026-08-26T14:42:05Z","authors":[{"email":"320962924+quuu824016[bot]@users.noreply.github.com","id":"BOT_kgDOEyGBbA","login":"quuu824016[bot]","name":"quuu824016[bot]"}],"committedDate":"2026-08-26T14:42:05Z","messageBody":"The workflow now says what it runs rather than hiding formatting and static
analysis behind one composer lint, pins every action to the commit it
resolves to, and grants nothing beyond reading the repository.

The version matrix asks whether the suite passes on each supported PHP.
Whether it survives being split across processes is a different question
and does not depend on the version, so the parallel runner is asked once,
on the highest one.

Mutation testing is handed a coverage report generated by the project's own
PHPUnit configuration. Infection's own initial run stops at the first byte
on STDERR and adds stopOnDefect, so one risky test would leave the gate
scoring a near-empty report as though it had scored everything. Memory is
sized for the report rather than the run, which is where it was exhausted
before, and a pull request is scored on the lines it changed against the
bar the toolkit sets for new code.","messageHeadline":"Make every gate a step you can read, and score mutants against a report","oid":"25ec25eced76eb7eceb9d83b5606eca2c2411c82"},{"authoredDate":"2026-08-26T14:58:51Z","authors":[{"email":"320962924+quuu824016[bot]@users.noreply.github.com","id":"BOT_kgDOEyGBbA","login":"quuu824016[bot]","name":"quuu824016[bot]"}],"committedDate":"2026-08-26T14:58:51Z","messageBody":"A test handed a real Faker can only check that something plausible came
out, and a range one short at either end still produces plausible output
every time. Every spelling the three realizers choose between is now
written down, and so is the range each choice was made from, which is what
makes a change to either of them show up as a failing test rather than as
output that still looks fine.

SQLite's character-class samples are the evidence that a compiled profile
covers the tokenizer rather than only the parts a grammar reaches. They

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>","messageHeadline":"Declare what the new tests read, and stop claiming a fixture is covered","oid":"c46b03771101de83b339d087d464758120e10956"},{"authoredDate":"2026-08-27T06:58:15Z","authors":[{"email":"320962924+quuu824016[bot]@users.noreply.github.com","id":"BOT_kgDOEyGBbA","login":"quuu824016[bot]","name":"quuu824016[bot]"},{"email":"noreply@anthropic.com","id":"MDQ6VXNlcjgxODQ3","login":"claude","name":"Claude Opus 5"}],"committedDate":"2026-08-27T06:58:15Z","messageBody":"The catalogue is the evidence the generator stands on: every terminal it
may write, the text that was observed to lex into it, and the upstream
scanner rule or lexer state that text reaches. Everything downstream
believes it. Nothing until now read one back.

The tests reached the builders only through the failure paths, so the
catalogue those builders assemble was exercised without being examined.
A sample could lose a token from what it claims to read as, a witness
could lose the rule it is the only evidence for, and an identifier could
lose the prefix that tells a reader which engine and which kind of
witness it is, and every test still passed.

Read the assembled catalogue: the parser modes and their units, the one
unit per scanner rule and per mode, the samples with their text, tokens
and units, and the keyword, lookahead and punctuation witnesses.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>","messageHeadline":"Read the catalogue back, rather than trusting it was written","oid":"581e4dc50ab735fa94f731fd8a3f2be7bf7d030a"},{"authoredDate":"2026-08-27T15:26:13Z","authors":[{"email":"320962924+quuu824016[bot]@users.noreply.github.com","id":"BOT_kgDOEyGBbA","login":"quuu824016[bot]","name":"quuu824016[bot]"},{"email":"noreply@anthropic.com","id":"MDQ6VXNlcjgxODQ3","login":"claude","name":"Claude Opus 5"}],"committedDate":"2026-08-27T15:26:13Z","messageBody":"The five PHP versions this package supports resolve four different
PHPUnit majors, and one configuration file had to serve all of them. A
setting any one major rejects makes the file invalid there, so the file
could only ever hold what the oldest accepts -- which meant three strict
settings the toolkit asks for were set on no version at all: complete
arrays in failure output, deprecations narrowed to first-party code, and
mock objects that cannot still take a call nobody planned.

Give each major the file written for it and name that file in the job
that installs it. The settings now apply wherever the major supports
them, rather than nowhere.

Sealing mocks is the one that needed the tests to change. A sealed mock
is one that cannot answer a call it was never told about, and PHPUnit's
way of sealing it does not exist on the older majors this package still
runs on. So the doubles that were verifying calls are now written out:
each records what it was asked, and the test reads that afterwards
instead of describing it in advance. That says the same thing, reads
more plainly, and holds on every major.

{"author":{"is_bot":true,"login":"app/quuu824016"},"baseRefName":"feat/ci-scope-pr-triggers","body":"Adopts `k-kinzal/php-ai-toolkit` in `packages/sql-faker`.

PHPStan is clean at level max with the toolkit's rules, the unit suite is green on PHP 8.1
through 8.5, and the mutation gate passes on the changed lines.

## Worth a look

- The grammar reader was split into named collaborators: `Grammar/SourceCursor`,
  `Grammar/Derivation`, `Grammar/TerminationCost`, `Grammar/LexicalProfileWriter`, and the
  `LexicalCatalogShape` / `LexicalWitnessShape` pair that say what a compiled profile is.
- The Bison and PostgreSQL grammar readers gained collaborators of their own, so reading a
  directive, a preamble or a start symbol each has an owner.
- Refusals are `GrammarParseException` / `GenerationException` / `LexicalCatalogException`
  rather than `InvalidArgumentException`, so a caller can catch what this package refuses
  without catching everything.

## Stack

Nine stacked PRs, one per package. Merge bottom-up:

1. #281 `sql-faker`
2. #282 `sql-fixture`
3. #283 `ztd-query-core`
4. #284 `ztd-query-mysql`
5. #285 `ztd-query-postgres`
6. #286 `ztd-query-sqlite`
7. #287 `ztd-query-pdo-adapter`
8. #288 `ztd-query-mysqli-adapter`
9. #289 `drop-custom-rules` — deletes `packages/phpstan-custom-rules`

A PR lower in the stack also triggers the workflows of the packages downstream of it,
because their `paths` filters name the package it changes; those downstream workflows stay
red until their own PR lands. #289 sits on top of the whole stack and is the one that shows
every package green at once — it is currently green on all 109 checks.

## What the toolkit changed, in every package

- `phpstan.neon` — `k-kinzal/phpstan-custom-rules` replaced by the toolkit's
  `extension.neon` and `rules.neon` alongside `phpstan-strict-rules`, at `level: max`.
- `.php-cs-fixer.dist.php` — byte-identical to the toolkit's template.
- `phpunit.xml.dist` — the toolkit's strict configuration and `AiTestReporterExtension`.
- `infection.json5` — the toolkit's thresholds, `maxTimeouts: 0`, `timeoutsAsEscaped`.
- `.github/workflows/<package>.yml` — the shape the toolkit's GitHub Actions and Infection
  skills ask for: actions pinned to commit SHAs, `permissions: contents: read`, per-job
  `timeout-minutes`, every gate a named step, a parallel-runner job, and a mutation job
  that pre-generates coverage and scores a pull request on its changed lines against
  `--min-msi=85 --min-covered-msi=85`.

## What the rules asked for, and what that meant

The toolkit forbids private and non-override protected methods, wants a paired unit test
for every public method, forbids `mixed` in any internal or scope-restricted declaration,
forbids catching `Throwable`/`Exception`, and wants a `@throws` tag for every checked
exception that escapes. Satisfying that is a design change rather than an annotation pass:
each private method either became a collaborator with a name and a test or became part of
its type's stated contract, and each `mixed` either got a named `@phpstan-type` on a public
boundary or was validated where it entered.

The last two were private methods, so the interesting decision — which
SQLSTATEs a schema-less run is allowed to hit — was reachable only through
the target's __invoke().

The seed derivation is identical in all three and is now CorpusSeed. The
dialect decision moves to MySqlSyntaxCheck, PgSyntaxCheck and
SqliteSyntaxCheck, each with a verify() that states in its @throws what a
failure means. PostgreSQL's bracketed-indirection exception was itself a
second decision inside the first, so it becomes PgBracketIndirection.

Two behaviours changed rather than moved. The empty catch around the plain
ROLLBACK swallowed a failure that left the connection in an unknown state;
it now reports on stderr, as does the savepoint rollback that precedes it.
The Error raised for an unexpected rejection now chains the PDOException it
came from, so the driver's own message survives in the fuzzer's report.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>","messageHeadline":"refactor(sql-faker): let the fuzz harness own its dialect checks","oid":"e3fa47395deb37c05d84dad3c49ef14c12bd7d4c"},{"authoredDate":"2026-08-24T10:04:48Z","authors":[{"email":"319849249+quuuai[bot]@users.noreply.github.com","id":"BOT_kgDOExCDIQ","login":"quuuai[bot]","name":"quuuai[bot]"},{"email":"noreply@anthropic.com","id":"MDQ6VXNlcjgxODQ3","login":"claude","name":"Claude Opus 5"}],"committedDate":"2026-08-24T10:04:48Z","messageBody":"The toolkit reports a PHPDoc block written on a single line: a tag crammed
onto the same line as its delimiters is easy to miss when reading and easy
to drop a second tag from when editing. Every such block in src and tests is
rewritten with /** and */ on their own lines.

The rest is the new PHP-CS-Fixer set applying itself — single-quoted
strings, alphabetically ordered imports, imported global classes and
functions, and trailing commas in multi-line calls. No behaviour changes.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>","messageHeadline":"style(sql-faker): expand one-line PHPDoc and apply the wider fixer set","oid":"8bfb6161b1d5789c881a5ff9dc843b839f030630"},{"authoredDate":"2026-08-24T10:15:57Z","authors":[{"email":"319849249+quuuai[bot]@users.noreply.github.com","id":"BOT_kgDOExCDIQ","login":"quuuai[bot]","name":"quuuai[bot]"},{"email":"noreply@anthropic.com","id":"MDQ6VXNlcjgxODQ3","login":"claude","name":"Claude Opus 5"}],"committedDate":"2026-08-24T10:15:57Z","messageBody":"…r errors

The generators and grammar parsers reported every failure as a
LogicException, and LexicalException extended one too. That put "this
grammar file declares no rules", "this rule cannot be realized" and "this
SQL did not round-trip" in the same family as a violated precondition —
failures a caller is told to fix rather than handle. sql-faker reads Bison
and Lemon grammars that ship with the servers it targets and tokenizes SQL
it was handed, so all three are runtime conditions.

LexicalException now extends RuntimeException, and two new types carry the
rest: GrammarParseException for source text that yields no rules, and
GenerationException for a grammar that cannot derive a statement. Both are
recoverable, so a caller generating from a grammar it did not author can
catch them without also swallowing its own bugs.

The wording moves onto the exceptions as named constructors. The same eight
messages were spelled out across the MySQL, PostgreSQL and SQLite
generators, twice with wording that had drifted apart: SQLite named the
empty rule where the others did not, and MySQL said "derivation plan" where
the others said "generation plan". Both now report the more useful form.

Precondition guards are untouched: GenerationPlan, Grammar and
RandomStringGenerator still raise InvalidArgumentException when a caller
passes an empty rule name or an empty catalog, because those are defects at
the call site.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>","messageHeadline":"refactor(sql-faker): make grammar failures recoverable, not programme…","oid":"2be765e243e249f606a6060c7652b782d5d6a98a"},{"authoredDate":"2026-08-24T10:28:47Z","authors":[{"email":"319849249+quuuai[bot]@users.noreply.github.com","id":"BOT_kgDOExCDIQ","login":"quuuai[bot]","name":"quuuai[bot]"},{"email":"noreply@anthropic.com","id":"MDQ6VXNlcjgxODQ3","login":"claude","name":"Claude Opus 5"}],"committedDate":"2026-08-24T10:28:47Z","messageBody":"The toolkit rejects four habits the suite had picked up, and each one hid a
test that could not fail for the reason it claimed to.

Twelve cases expected an InvalidArgumentException or a LogicException from a
precondition guard: an empty rule name, an empty lexeme catalog, a zero-part
hostname. Those are defects at the call site, so the test only asserted that
broken input breaks. They are deleted; the guards they poked at stay.

Fifteen more asserted a class implements an interface or extends an
exception, which the engine already guarantees and no change to the class
body can break. Deleted too, along with the three-line variant that checked
the same thing for all three dialect lexers. PgGrammar::load() and
SqliteGrammar::load() kept their tests but now assert the loaded grammar has
rules, which is what a caller actually depends on.

Seven read method signatures through Reflection to check default argument
values. The contract they were reaching for is that calling with no
arguments matches calling with those values, so they now assert exactly
that, against one re-seeded generator. Two interface tests that asked
Reflection whether an interface is an interface now exercise the contract:
every Symbol reports its own value, and every Bison declaration kind can be
carried by an AST.

Test methods named after constructors are renamed for the behaviour they
pin down, and the anonymous Faker stubs declare the exception they throw.

Three Reflection uses remain in the SQLite generator tests. They read the
private augmented grammar, and they go away when that augmentation becomes a
collaborator with an API of its own.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>","messageHeadline":"test(sql-faker): assert behaviour instead of shape","oid":"509ce33dd7c6b1fcf358c44dd874241cb0b38ee9"},{"authoredDate":"2026-08-24T11:51:57Z","authors":[{"email":"320539145+quuu143225[bot]@users.noreply.github.com","id":"BOT_kgDOExsKCQ","login":"quuu143225[bot]","name":"quuu143225[bot]"},{"email":"noreply@anthropic.com","id":"MDQ6VXNlcjgxODQ3","login":"claude","name":"Claude Opus 5"}],"committedDate":"2026-08-24T11:51:57Z","messageBody":"BisonLexer had twenty-four private methods, and they were private for one
reason: every one of them read and moved $this->pos. Six were cursor
primitives, sixteen were the states of the scan, and the rest were a
lookahead buffer the parser needs. None of them could be reached without
also owning the position, so the interesting rules — what closes a
brace-delimited action, what a prologue does when the file is truncated —
were only observable by feeding a whole grammar file to next().

The position now belongs to SourceCursor, which every state receives as an
argument instead of reaching into. That is what removes the private
modifier; moving the same bodies onto another class would only have replaced
one shared field with a longer parameter list.

Each state is a BisonScanner that declares the character it starts on and
returns the token it read: DirectiveScanner, ActionScanner, TypeTagScanner,
QuotedLiteralScanner, NumberScanner, IdentifierScanner, PunctuationScanner.
BisonScannerChain holds the order, so the lexer dispatches by lookup and no
scanner knows the others exist. BisonTokenStream carries the lookahead, which
keeps the lexer a forward scan that never re-reads a token.

Trivia is not a scanner. Whitespace and comments may sit between any two
lexemes, so modelling them as lexemes would mean every scanner having to
answer "nothing this time" and the lexer looping until one of them did not.
BisonTrivia skips them before dispatch, which is what lets scan() promise a
token rather than a token-or-null, and turns the old recursion through
token() into a single pass. It also owns the one place a slash is not a
comment: inside an action body a slash is division, so recognising a comment
and requiring one are separate operations.

BisonTokenType is renamed BisonLexeme: it names what was read, not a type.

Two failures change shape. Unreadable grammar source now raises
GrammarParseException rather than a bare RuntimeException, and peekN() below
one raises InvalidArgumentException, because asking for the zeroth token
ahead is a defect in the caller rather than in the grammar.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>","messageHeadline":"refactor(sql-faker): make the Bison lexer's states explicit","oid":"159b8bc4462c60861202f1bfd198cf82ddd297fc"},{"authoredDate":"2026-08-24T13:35:02Z","authors":[{"email":"320539145+quuu143225[bot]@users.noreply.github.com","id":"BOT_kgDOExsKCQ","login":"quuu143225[bot]","name":"quuu143225[bot]"},{"email":"noreply@anthropic.com","id":"MDQ6VXNlcjgxODQ3","login":"claude","name":"Claude Opus 5"}],"committedDate":"2026-08-24T13:35:02Z","messageBody":"BisonParser held twenty private methods and three responsibilities: the
order of a grammar file's sections, the argument shape of each of the eight
declaration kinds, and how a rule's alternatives are assembled. They were
private because each one advanced a shared token stream, so `%define` could
only be exercised by handing a whole grammar file to parse().

The eight declaration shapes are eight different grammars — `%expect` takes
a number, `%token` takes names with optional codes and aliases,
`%parse-param` takes a block of host code — so each becomes a
BisonDirectiveReader that answers for its own directive.
BisonDirectiveReaderChain holds the routing, and the reader for directives
this parser has no model for sits last, which is what keeps an unrecognised
directive from swallowing the declarations after it. Where a declaration
ends was decided in four places by one predicate; it is now
BisonDeclarationBoundary, so those four cannot drift apart.

The rules section splits the same way. BisonRuleReader finds the rules,
BisonAlternativeReader reads one rule's alternatives, and the alternative
being read is BisonAlternativeDraft rather than five local variables that
had to be reset at each of the three places an alternative can end — the
place a forgotten reset would have attached one alternative's action to the
next. BisonPreambleReader and BisonStartSymbol carry what is left.

Readers were written as peek-then-consume, and PHPStan reported the result:
having narrowed the peeked lexeme, it could not see that consuming a token
changes it, so four comparisons looked constant. The stream was missing the
operation the readers actually wanted, and nextIf() is it — take the next
token only if it is one of these kinds. Reading a type tag, a token code or
an alias is now one step that cannot look at one token and consume another,
and the coercion those readers repeated moves onto BisonToken as asString()
and asInt().

BisonSymbolType becomes BisonSymbolForm and BisonTokenInfo becomes
BisonTokenDefinition: one records how a symbol was written, the other is a
terminal a %token directive declares.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>","messageHeadline":"refactor(sql-faker): give the Bison parser one reader per thing it reads","oid":"36d2369128f2bd67376c234ed0b0607b88d575b6"},{"authoredDate":"2026-08-24T13:48:55Z","authors":[{"email":"320539145+quuu143225[bot]@users.noreply.github.com","id":"BOT_kgDOExsKCQ","login":"quuu143225[bot]","name":"quuu143225[bot]"},{"email":"noreply@anthropic.com","id":"MDQ6VXNlcjgxODQ3","login":"claude","name":"Claude Opus 5"}],"committedDate":"2026-08-24T13:48:55Z","messageBody":"LexicalCatalog was two things: the validated catalog its callers ask
questions of, and the reading that turns a decoded resource file into one.
The reading was three private methods and thirty-one throw sites, fourteen
of which raised the same sentence — so a catalog regenerated from a changed
upstream lexer failed with "Invalid upstream lexical catalog shape." and no
indication of which field had moved.

Reading is now LexicalCatalogShape, section by section, with
LexicalWitnessShape for the individual lexing examples and their two
spellings. The two agreement checks are LexicalCoverageCheck, which holds the
partition rule — every unit of the upstream lexer witnessed or excluded,
never both and never neither — and LexicalWitnessCheck, which holds the
rule that the catalog' two halves refer back to each other. LexicalCatalog
keeps only the questions.

The thirty-one messages become LexicalCatalogException, one named
constructor per way the file can be wrong, and the shape failures now name
the field: "Field: coverage.witnessed" rather than the same sentence again.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>","messageHeadline":"refactor(sql-faker): read the terminal catalog before trusting it","oid":"763a170656747a3c390fda32f6a19c24a1724fdc"},{"authoredDate":"2026-08-24T14:15:03Z","authors":[{"email":"320539145+quuu143225[bot]@users.noreply.github.com","id":"BOT_kgDOExsKCQ","login":"quuu143225[bot]","name":"quuu143225[bot]"},{"email":"noreply@anthropic.com","id":"MDQ6VXNlcjgxODQ3","login":"claude","name":"Claude Opus 5"}],"committedDate":"2026-08-24T14:15:03Z","messageBody":"… back

MySql\LexicalGrammar held two inverse operations. Realization turns a
terminal into SQL; tokenizing turns SQL back into terminals; the class did
both and compared the results, so eighteen private methods belonging to one
side or the other shared a class with no way to reach either alone. Testing
that a run of digits widens from NUM to LONG_NUM at the right magnitude
meant generating a statement that happened to contain one.

MySqlTokenizer now owns reading, MySqlTerminalRealizer owns writing, and
LexicalGrammar owns the round trip that makes the pair worth having. The
tokenizer's rules are separate methods in the order the server applies them,
so the one that depends on what came before it — a hostname is a hostname
because an `@` preceded it — says so in its signature.

Three things the dialects were repeating move to SqlFaker\Grammar.
LexicalProfileSource loads a profile and refuses one that names a different
server than the caller asked for. LexicalKeywordIndex inverts the profile's
terminal-to-spelling map. A
read that leaves the offset where it was has not read anything, and the

Each loop now checks that it got somewhere and refuses when it did not, so
a lexer that cannot make progress says which offset it is stuck at.","messageHeadline":"Refuse a scan that has not got anywhere","oid":"e4c440365499edde5f0077cdb32bba7a3ae6044e"},{"authoredDate":"2026-08-26T16:02:59Z","authors":[{"email":"320962924+quuu824016[bot]@users.noreply.github.com","id":"BOT_kgDOEyGBbA","login":"quuu824016[bot]","name":"quuu824016[bot]"}],"committedDate":"2026-08-26T16:02:59Z","messageBody":"Joining WITH ROLLUP walked an index it also spliced under, which is the one
shape of loop a change to the arithmetic turns into a hang rather than a
failure. It reads the tokens once now and writes the joined ones out.

The mutation timeout is measured rather than assumed. A mutant that removes

limit still stops it — but it walks a far larger derivation on the way, and
those runs take longer than the bar the timeout was set at. Reporting them
as escaped said something about the clock rather than about the tests.","messageHeadline":"Merge tokens without an index that could run away, and time the gate","oid":"1f3b4738d313801de994691a76f2c41b3b74d62b"},{"authoredDate":"2026-08-26T16:33:12Z","authors":[{"email":"320962924+quuu824016[bot]@users.noreply.github.com","id":"BOT_kgDOEyGBbA","login":"quuu824016[bot]","name":"quuu824016[bot]"}],"committedDate":"2026-08-26T16:33:12Z","messageBody":"…ource

Opus 5"}],"committedDate":"2026-08-27T05:51:05Z","messageBody":"The coverage run is strict about metadata, so a test that touches a
class it has not named is an error rather than a note. Two kinds of that
error crept in with the new tests.

The profile builder tests read the lexical sample catalogues to decide
what a profile should contain, and had not said so. Name them.

The lexer test drives a scanner that exists only under tests, and had
named it as used. A fixture is not in the measured source, so there is
no coverage record to attach it to and the run rejects the claim. Drop
it; the classes it does cover are still listed.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>","messageHeadline":"Declare what the new tests read, and stop claiming a fixture is covered","oid":"c46b03771101de83b339d087d464758120e10956"},{"authoredDate":"2026-08-27T06:58:15Z","authors":[{"email":"320962924+quuu824016[bot]@users.noreply.github.com","id":"BOT_kgDOEyGBbA","login":"quuu824016[bot]","name":"quuu824016[bot]"},{"email":"noreply@anthropic.com","id":"MDQ6VXNlcjgxODQ3","login":"claude","name":"Claude Opus 5"}],"committedDate":"2026-08-27T06:58:15Z","messageBody":"The catalogue is the evidence the generator stands on: every terminal it
may write, the text that was observed to lex into it, and the upstream
scanner rule or lexer state that text reaches. Everything downstream
believes it. Nothing until now read one back.

The tests reached the builders only through the failure paths, so the
catalogue those builders assemble was exercised without being examined.
A sample could lose a token from what it claims to read as, a witness
could lose the rule it is the only evidence for, and an identifier could
lose the prefix that tells a reader which engine and which kind of
witness it is, and every test still passed.

Read the assembled catalogue: the parser modes and their units, the one
unit per scanner rule and per mode, the samples with their text, tokens
and units, and the keyword, lookahead and punctuation witnesses.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>","messageHeadline":"Read the catalogue back, rather than trusting it was written","oid":"581e4dc50ab735fa94f731fd8a3f2be7bf7d030a"},{"authoredDate":"2026-08-27T15:26:13Z","authors":[{"email":"320962924+quuu824016[bot]@users.noreply.github.com","id":"BOT_kgDOEyGBbA","login":"quuu824016[bot]","name":"quuu824016[bot]"},{"email":"noreply@anthropic.com","id":"MDQ6VXNlcjgxODQ3","login":"claude","name":"Claude Opus 5"}],"committedDate":"2026-08-27T15:26:13Z","messageBody":"The five PHP versions this package supports resolve four different
PHPUnit majors, and one configuration file had to serve all of them. A
setting any one major rejects makes the file invalid there, so the file
could only ever hold what the oldest accepts -- which meant three strict
settings the toolkit asks for were set on no version at all: complete
arrays in failure output, deprecations narrowed to first-party code, and
mock objects that cannot still take a call nobody planned.

Give each major the file written for it and name that file in the job
that installs it. The settings now apply wherever the major supports
them, rather than nowhere.

Sealing mocks is the one that needed the tests to change. A sealed mock
is one that cannot answer a call it was never told about, and PHPUnit's
way of sealing it does not exist on the older majors this package still
runs on. So the doubles that were verifying calls are now written out:
each records what it was asked, and the test reads that afterwards
instead of describing it in advance. That says the same thing, reads
more plainly, and holds on every major.

{"author":{"is_bot":true,"login":"app/quuu824016"},"baseRefName":"feat/ci-scope-pr-triggers","body":"Adopts `k-kinzal/php-ai-toolkit` in `packages/sql-faker`.

PHPStan is clean at level max with the toolkit's rules, the unit suite is green on PHP 8.1
through 8.5, and the mutation gate passes on the changed lines.

## Worth a look

- The grammar reader was split into named collaborators: `Grammar/SourceCursor`,
  `Grammar/Derivation`, `Grammar/TerminationCost`, `Grammar/LexicalProfileWriter`, and the
  `LexicalCatalogShape` / `LexicalWitnessShape` pair that say what a compiled profile is.
- The Bison and PostgreSQL grammar readers gained collaborators of their own, so reading a
  directive, a preamble or a start symbol each has an owner.
- Refusals are `GrammarParseException` / `GenerationException` / `LexicalCatalogException`
  rather than `InvalidArgumentException`, so a caller can catch what this package refuses
  without catching everything.

## Stack

Nine stacked PRs, one per package. Merge bottom-up:

1. #281 `sql-faker`
2. #282 `sql-fixture`
3. #283 `ztd-query-core`
4. #284 `ztd-query-mysql`
5. #285 `ztd-query-postgres`
6. #286 `ztd-query-sqlite`
7. #287 `ztd-query-pdo-adapter`
8. #288 `ztd-query-mysqli-adapter`
9. #289 `drop-custom-rules` — deletes `packages/phpstan-custom-rules`

A PR lower in the stack also triggers the workflows of the packages downstream of it,
because their `paths` filters name the package it changes; those downstream workflows stay
red until their own PR lands. #289 sits on top of the whole stack and is the one that shows
every package green at once — it is currently green on all 109 checks.

## What the toolkit changed, in every package

- `phpstan.neon` — `k-kinzal/phpstan-custom-rules` replaced by the toolkit's
  `extension.neon` and `rules.neon` alongside `phpstan-strict-rules`, at `level: max`.
- `.php-cs-fixer.dist.php` — byte-identical to the toolkit's template.
- `phpunit.xml.dist` — the toolkit's strict configuration and `AiTestReporterExtension`.
- `infection.json5` — the toolkit's thresholds, `maxTimeouts: 0`, `timeoutsAsEscaped`.
- `.github/workflows/<package>.yml` — the shape the toolkit's GitHub Actions and Infection
  skills ask for: actions pinned to commit SHAs, `permissions: contents: read`, per-job
  `timeout-minutes`, every gate a named step, a parallel-runner job, and a mutation job
  that pre-generates coverage and scores a pull request on its changed lines against
  `--min-msi=85 --min-covered-msi=85`.

## What the rules asked for, and what that meant

The toolkit forbids private and non-override protected methods, wants a paired unit test
for every public method, forbids `mixed` in any internal or scope-restricted declaration,
forbids catching `Throwable`/`Exception`, and wants a `@throws` tag for every checked
exception that escapes. Satisfying that is a design change rather than an annotation pass:
each private method either became a collaborator with a name and a test or became part of
its type's stated contract, and each `mixed` either got a named `@phpstan-type` on a public
boundary or was validated where it entered.

The generators and grammar parsers reported every failure as a
LogicException, and LexicalException extended one too. That put "this
grammar file declares no rules", "this rule cannot be realized" and "this
SQL did not round-trip" in the same family as a violated precondition —
failures a caller is told to fix rather than handle. sql-faker reads Bison
and Lemon grammars that ship with the servers it targets and tokenizes SQL
it was handed, so all three are runtime conditions.

LexicalException now extends RuntimeException, and two new types carry the
rest: GrammarParseException for source text that yields no rules, and
GenerationException for a grammar that cannot derive a statement. Both are
recoverable, so a caller generating from a grammar it did not author can
catch them without also swallowing its own bugs.

The wording moves onto the exceptions as named constructors. The same eight
messages were spelled out across the MySQL, PostgreSQL and SQLite
generators, twice with wording that had drifted apart: SQLite named the
empty rule where the others did not, and MySQL said "derivation plan" where
the others said "generation plan". Both now report the more useful form.

Precondition guards are untouched: GenerationPlan, Grammar and
RandomStringGenerator still raise InvalidArgumentException when a caller
passes an empty rule name or an empty catalog, because those are defects at
the call site.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>","messageHeadline":"refactor(sql-faker): make grammar failures recoverable, not programme…","oid":"2be765e243e249f606a6060c7652b782d5d6a98a"},{"authoredDate":"2026-08-24T10:28:47Z","authors":[{"email":"319849249+quuuai[bot]@users.noreply.github.com","id":"BOT_kgDOExCDIQ","login":"quuuai[bot]","name":"quuuai[bot]"},{"email":"noreply@anthropic.com","id":"MDQ6VXNlcjgxODQ3","login":"claude","name":"Claude Opus 5"}],"committedDate":"2026-08-24T10:28:47Z","messageBody":"The toolkit rejects four habits the suite had picked up, and each one hid a
test that could not fail for the reason it claimed to.

Twelve cases expected an InvalidArgumentException or a LogicException from a
precondition guard: an empty rule name, an empty lexeme catalog, a zero-part
hostname. Those are defects at the call site, so the test only asserted that
broken input breaks. They are deleted; the guards they poked at stay.

Fifteen more asserted a class implements an interface or extends an
exception, which the engine already guarantees and no change to the class
body can break. Deleted too, along with the three-line variant that checked
the same thing for all three dialect lexers. PgGrammar::load() and
SqliteGrammar::load() kept their tests but now assert the loaded grammar has
rules, which is what a caller actually depends on.

Seven read method signatures through Reflection to check default argument
values. The contract they were reaching for is that calling with no
arguments matches calling with those values, so they now assert exactly
that, against one re-seeded generator. Two interface tests that asked
Reflection whether an interface is an interface now exercise the contract:
every Symbol reports its own value, and every Bison declaration kind can be
carried by an AST.

Test methods named after constructors are renamed for the behaviour they
pin down, and the anonymous Faker stubs declare the exception they throw.

Three Reflection uses remain in the SQLite generator tests. They read the
private augmented grammar, and they go away when that augmentation becomes a
collaborator with an API of its own.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>","messageHeadline":"test(sql-faker): assert behaviour instead of shape","oid":"509ce33dd7c6b1fcf358c44dd874241cb0b38ee9"},{"authoredDate":"2026-08-24T11:51:57Z","authors":[{"email":"320539145+quuu143225[bot]@users.noreply.github.com","id":"BOT_kgDOExsKCQ","login":"quuu143225[bot]","name":"quuu143225[bot]"},{"email":"noreply@anthropic.com","id":"MDQ6VXNlcjgxODQ3","login":"claude","name":"Claude Opus 5"}],"committedDate":"2026-08-24T11:51:57Z","messageBody":"BisonLexer had twenty-four private methods, and they were private for one
reason: every one of them read and moved $this->pos. Six were cursor
primitives, sixteen were the states of the scan, and the rest were a
lookahead buffer the parser needs. None of them could be reached without
also owning the position, so the interesting rules — what closes a
brace-delimited action, what a prologue does when the file is truncated —
were only observable by feeding a whole grammar file to next().

The position now belongs to SourceCursor, which every state receives as an
argument instead of reaching into. That is what removes the private
modifier; moving the same bodies onto another class would only have replaced
one shared field with a longer parameter list.

Each state is a BisonScanner that declares the character it starts on and
returns the token it read: DirectiveScanner, ActionScanner, TypeTagScanner,
QuotedLiteralScanner, NumberScanner, IdentifierScanner, PunctuationScanner.
BisonScannerChain holds the order, so the lexer dispatches by lookup and no
scanner knows the others exist. BisonTokenStream carries the lookahead, which
keeps the lexer a forward scan that never re-reads a token.

Trivia is not a scanner. Whitespace and comments may sit between any two
lexemes, so modelling them as lexemes would mean every scanner having to
answer "nothing this time" and the lexer looping until one of them did not.
BisonTrivia skips them before dispatch, which is what lets scan() promise a
token rather than a token-or-null, and turns the old recursion through
token() into a single pass. It also owns the one place a slash is not a
comment: inside an action body a slash is division, so recognising a comment
and requiring one are separate operations.

BisonTokenType is renamed BisonLexeme: it names what was read, not a type.

Two failures change shape. Unreadable grammar source now raises
GrammarParseException rather than a bare RuntimeException, and peekN() below
one raises InvalidArgumentException, because asking for the zeroth token
ahead is a defect in the caller rather than in the grammar.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>","messageHeadline":"refactor(sql-faker): make the Bison lexer's states explicit","oid":"159b8bc4462c60861202f1bfd198cf82ddd297fc"},{"authoredDate":"2026-08-24T13:35:02Z","authors":[{"email":"320539145+quuu143225[bot]@users.noreply.github.com","id":"BOT_kgDOExsKCQ","login":"quuu143225[bot]","name":"quuu143225[bot]"},{"email":"noreply@anthropic.com","id":"MDQ6VXNlcjgxODQ3","login":"claude","name":"Claude Opus 5"}],"committedDate":"2026-08-24T13:35:02Z","messageBody":"BisonParser held twenty private methods and three responsibilities: the
order of a grammar file's sections, the argument shape of each of the eight
declaration kinds, and how a rule's alternatives are assembled. They were
private because each one advanced a shared token stream, so `%define` could
only be exercised by handing a whole grammar file to parse().

The eight declaration shapes are eight different grammars — `%expect` takes
a number, `%token` takes names with optional codes and aliases,
`%parse-param` takes a block of host code — so each becomes a
BisonDirectiveReader that answers for its own directive.
BisonDirectiveReaderChain holds the routing, and the reader for directives
this parser has no model for sits last, which is what keeps an unrecognised
directive from swallowing the declarations after it. Where a declaration
ends was decided in four places by one predicate; it is now
BisonDeclarationBoundary, so those four cannot drift apart.

The rules section splits the same way. BisonRuleReader finds the rules,
BisonAlternativeReader reads one rule's alternatives, and the alternative
being read is BisonAlternativeDraft rather than five local variables that
had to be reset at each of the three places an alternative can end — the
place a forgotten reset would have attached one alternative's action to the
next. BisonPreambleReader and BisonStartSymbol carry what is left.

Readers were written as peek-then-consume, and PHPStan reported the result:
having narrowed the peeked lexeme, it could not see that consuming a token
changes it, so four comparisons looked constant. The stream was missing the
operation the readers actually wanted, and nextIf() is it — take the next
token only if it is one of these kinds. Reading a type tag, a token code or
an alias is now one step that cannot look at one token and consume another,
and the coercion those readers repeated moves onto BisonToken as asString()
and asInt().

BisonSymbolType becomes BisonSymbolForm and BisonTokenInfo becomes
BisonTokenDefinition: one records how a symbol was written, the other is a
terminal a %token directive declares.

The reading was three private methods and thirty-one throw sites, fourteen
of which raised the same sentence — so a catalog regenerated from a changed
upstream lexer failed with "Invalid upstream lexical catalog shape." and no
indication of which field had moved.

Reading is now LexicalCatalogShape, section by section, with
LexicalWitnessShape for the individual lexing examples and their two
spellings. The two agreement checks are LexicalCoverageCheck, which holds the
partition rule — every unit of the upstream lexer witnessed or excluded,
never both and never neither — and LexicalWitnessCheck, which holds the
rule that the catalog' two halves refer back to each other. LexicalCatalog
keeps only the questions.

The thirty-one messages become LexicalCatalogException, one named
constructor per way the file can be wrong, and the shape failures now name
the field: "Field: coverage.witnessed" rather than the same sentence again.

MySql\LexicalGrammar held two inverse operations. Realization turns a
terminal into SQL; tokenizing turns SQL back into terminals; the class did
both and compared the results, so eighteen private methods belonging to one
side or the other shared a class with no way to reach either alone. Testing
that a run of digits widens from NUM to LONG_NUM at the right magnitude
meant generating a statement that happened to contain one.

MySqlTokenizer now owns reading, MySqlTerminalRealizer owns writing, and
LexicalGrammar owns the round trip that makes the pair worth having. The
tokenizer's rules are separate methods in the order the server applies them,
so the one that depends on what came before it — a hostname is a hostname
because an `@` preceded it — says so in its signature.

Three things the dialects were repeating move to SqlFaker\Grammar.
LexicalProfileSource loads a profile and refuses one that names a different
server than the caller asked for. LexicalKeywordIndex inverts the profile's
terminal-to-spelling map. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>","messageHeadline":"Declare what the new tests read, and stop claiming a fixture is covered","oid":"c46b03771101de83b339d087d464758120e10956"},{"authoredDate":"2026-08-27T06:58:15Z","authors":[{"email":"320962924+quuu824016[bot]@users.noreply.github.com","id":"BOT_kgDOEyGBbA","login":"quuu824016[bot]","name":"quuu824016[bot]"},{"email":"noreply@anthropic.com","id":"MDQ6VXNlcjgxODQ3","login":"claude","name":"Claude Opus 5"}],"committedDate":"2026-08-27T06:58:15Z","messageBody":"The catalogue is the evidence the generator stands on: every terminal it
may write, the text that was observed to lex into it, and the upstream
scanner rule or lexer state that text reaches. Everything downstream
believes it. Nothing until now read one back.

The tests reached the builders only through the failure paths, so the
catalogue those builders assemble was exercised without being examined.
A sample could lose a token from what it claims to read as, a witness
could lose the rule it is the only evidence for, and an identifier could
lose the prefix that tells a reader which engine and which kind of
witness it is, and every test still passed.

Read the assembled catalogue: the parser modes and their units, the one
unit per scanner rule and per mode, the samples with their text, tokens
and units, and the keyword, lookahead and punctuation witnesses.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>","messageHeadline":"Read the catalogue back, rather than trusting it was written","oid":"581e4dc50ab735fa94f731fd8a3f2be7bf7d030a"},{"authoredDate":"2026-08-27T15:26:13Z","authors":[{"email":"320962924+quuu824016[bot]@users.noreply.github.com","id":"BOT_kgDOEyGBbA","login":"quuu824016[bot]","name":"quuu824016[bot]"},{"email":"noreply@anthropic.com","id":"MDQ6VXNlcjgxODQ3","login":"claude","name":"Claude Opus 5"}],"committedDate":"2026-08-27T15:26:13Z","messageBody":"The five PHP versions this package supports resolve four different
PHPUnit majors, and one configuration file had to serve all of them. A
setting any one major rejects makes the file invalid there, so the file
could only ever hold what the oldest accepts -- which meant three strict
settings the toolkit asks for were set on no version at all: complete
arrays in failure output, deprecations narrowed to first-party code, and
mock objects that cannot still take a call nobody planned.

Give each major the file written for it and name that file in the job
that installs it. The settings now apply wherever the major supports
them, rather than nowhere.

Sealing mocks is the one that needed the tests to change. A sealed mock
is one that cannot answer a call it was never told about, and PHPUnit's
way of sealing it does not exist on the older majors this package still
runs on. So the doubles that were verifying calls are now written out:
each records what it was asked, and the test reads that afterwards
instead of describing it in advance. That says the same thing, reads
more plainly, and holds on every major.

        "bench:quick": "phpbench run bench --bootstrap=vendor/autoload.php --report=aggregate --php-config='{\"memory_limit\":\"512M\"}' --warmup=1 --iterations=3 --revs=25",
        "bench:full": "phpbench run bench --bootstrap=vendor/autoload.php --report=aggregate --php-config='{\"memory_limit\":\"512M\"}' --warmup=2 --iterations=8 --revs=100",

{
    "$schema": "vendor/infection/infection/resources/schema.json",
    // Measured, not guessed. This package generates SQL by walking a grammar, and a
    // mutant that removes a constraint from a generation plan does not hang — the
    // derivation step limit still stops it — but it wanders through a far larger
    // derivation first. Those runs were measured between 25 and roughly 60 seconds

    // this back would not make the suite stronger; it would report slow mutants as
    // escaped ones.

    // package, run to about three minutes together on the mutation runner, and a
    // mutant re-runs every test that covers it. One timed out at 90 seconds; ten

        "perMutator": "build/infection/per-mutator.md",

    "mutators": {

    "minMsi": 80,
    "minCoveredMsi": 80,
    "timeoutsAsEscaped": true,
    "maxTimeouts": 0,
    "tmpDir": "build/infection-tmp",
    "phpUnit": {
        "configDir": ".",
        "customPath": "vendor/bin/phpunit"

name: CI (sql-faker)

on:

    # package this one depends on is validated by that package's own workflow,
    # and by the push-to-main run below, which rebuilds every package against
    # the merged tree. Listing dependencies here instead would make a stacked
    # series unmergeable: the first pull request in the stack would have to
    # carry every later package's changes to keep this workflow passing.
    paths:
      - 'packages/sql-faker/**'
      - '.github/workflows/sql-faker.yml'

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.head_ref || github.ref_name }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

        # each other's strict settings, so every leg names the configuration
        # written for the major it will actually install.

          - php: '8.1'
            test-script: test:unit:10
          - php: '8.2'
            test-script: test:unit:11
          - php: '8.3'
            test-script: test:unit:12
          - php: '8.4'
            test-script: test:unit:12
          - php: '8.5'
            test-script: test:unit

      - name: Set up PHP ${{ matrix.php }}
        uses: shivammathur/setup-php@f3e473d116dcccaddc5834248c87452386958240 # 2.37.2
        with:
          php-version: ${{ matrix.php }}
          extensions: mbstring
          coverage: none

      - name: Install dependencies
        uses: ramsey/composer-install@65e4f84970763564f46a70b8a54b90d033b3bdda # 4.0.0
        with:
          working-directory: packages/sql-faker
          dependency-versions: highest
          composer-options: --prefer-dist

      - name: Check installed platform requirements
        run: composer check-platform-reqs

      - name: Unit tests
        run: composer ${{ matrix.test-script }}

  parallel-test:
    name: Parallel Test Runner
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 20
    steps:
      - name: Check out the repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

        uses: ramsey/composer-install@65e4f84970763564f46a70b8a54b90d033b3bdda # 4.0.0
        with:
          working-directory: packages/sql-faker
          dependency-versions: highest
          composer-options: --prefer-dist

      # split across processes. That does not depend on the PHP version, so it
      # is asked once, on the highest one supported.

        run: composer test

    name: Lint (PHP ${{ matrix.php }})
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 20
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        php: ['8.1', '8.2', '8.3', '8.4', '8.5']
    steps:
      - name: Check out the repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Set up PHP ${{ matrix.php }}
        uses: shivammathur/setup-php@f3e473d116dcccaddc5834248c87452386958240 # 2.37.2
        with:
          php-version: ${{ matrix.php }}
          extensions: mbstring

        uses: ramsey/composer-install@65e4f84970763564f46a70b8a54b90d033b3bdda # 4.0.0

          working-directory: packages/sql-faker
          dependency-versions: highest

  # question every time.

      - name: Set up PHP
        uses: shivammathur/setup-php@f3e473d116dcccaddc5834248c87452386958240 # 2.37.2

        uses: ramsey/composer-install@65e4f84970763564f46a70b8a54b90d033b3bdda # 4.0.0

          dependency-versions: highest

    name: Mutation Testing

    # that covers it, and the provider tests that cover most of it generate SQL
    # by walking a grammar. The ceiling is set well above the measured run so a

          --ignore-msi-with-no-mutations
          --min-msi=85
          --min-covered-msi=85

          coverage: none

      - name: Install dependencies
        uses: ramsey/composer-install@65e4f84970763564f46a70b8a54b90d033b3bdda # 4.0.0
        with:
          working-directory: packages/sql-faker
          dependency-versions: highest
          composer-options: --prefer-dist

      # What the version matrix cannot answer: whether the suite survives being
      # split across processes. That does not depend on the PHP version, so it
      # is asked once, on the highest one supported.
      - name: Unit tests, split across processes
        run: composer test

  lint:
    name: Lint (PHP ${{ matrix.php }})
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 20
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        php: ['8.1', '8.2', '8.3', '8.4', '8.5']
    steps:
      - name: Check out the repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Set up PHP ${{ matrix.php }}
        uses: shivammathur/setup-php@f3e473d116dcccaddc5834248c87452386958240 # 2.37.2
        with:
          php-version: ${{ matrix.php }}
          extensions: mbstring
          coverage: none

      - name: Install dependencies
        uses: ramsey/composer-install@65e4f84970763564f46a70b8a54b90d033b3bdda # 4.0.0
        with:
          working-directory: packages/sql-faker
          dependency-versions: highest
          composer-options: --prefer-dist

      - name: Validate composer.json
        run: composer validate --strict --no-check-publish

      - name: Coding standards
        run: composer format:check

  # PHPStan reads the language and the dependency graph of the runtime it runs
  # under, and a package supporting 8.1 through 8.5 has a different graph on
  # each: PHPUnit 10's attributes on 8.1, PHPUnit 13's on 8.5. Analysing once,
  # on the highest supported version, is the only way it can answer the same
  # question every time.
  static-analysis:
    name: Static Analysis
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 20
    steps:
      - name: Check out the repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Set up PHP
        uses: shivammathur/setup-php@f3e473d116dcccaddc5834248c87452386958240 # 2.37.2
        with:
          php-version: '8.5'
          extensions: mbstring
          coverage: none

      - name: Install dependencies
        uses: ramsey/composer-install@65e4f84970763564f46a70b8a54b90d033b3bdda # 4.0.0
        with:
          working-directory: packages/sql-faker
          dependency-versions: highest
          composer-options: --prefer-dist

      - name: Static analysis
        run: composer phpstan

  bench:
    name: Benchmark
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 20
    steps:
      - name: Check out the repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Set up PHP
        uses: shivammathur/setup-php@f3e473d116dcccaddc5834248c87452386958240 # 2.37.2
        with:
          php-version: '8.5'
          extensions: mbstring
          coverage: none

      - name: Install dependencies
        uses: ramsey/composer-install@65e4f84970763564f46a70b8a54b90d033b3bdda # 4.0.0
        with:
          working-directory: packages/sql-faker
          dependency-versions: highest
          composer-options: --prefer-dist

      - name: Benchmarks
        run: composer bench

  mutation:
    name: Mutation Testing
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # Scoring this package takes about half an hour: a mutant re-runs every test
    # that covers it, and the provider tests that cover most of it generate SQL
    # by walking a grammar. The ceiling is set well above the measured run so a
    # slow runner does not fail the build on the clock.
    timeout-minutes: 90
    steps:
      - name: Check out the repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          # Scoring a pull request means diffing it against its base branch,
          # which needs more than the single commit a shallow clone provides.
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Set up PHP
        uses: shivammathur/setup-php@f3e473d116dcccaddc5834248c87452386958240 # 2.37.2
        with:
          php-version: '8.5'
          extensions: mbstring, pcntl
          # Infection needs a coverage driver. pcov is several times faster than
          # Xdebug and Infection collects nothing Xdebug alone can provide.
          coverage: pcov

      - name: Install dependencies
        uses: ramsey/composer-install@65e4f84970763564f46a70b8a54b90d033b3bdda # 4.0.0
        with:
          working-directory: packages/sql-faker
          dependency-versions: highest
          composer-options: --prefer-dist

      - name: Check installed platform requirements
        run: composer check-platform-reqs

      # Infection's own initial test run cannot be used against a strict toolkit
      # PHPUnit configuration: it stops at the first byte on STDERR and adds
      # stopOnDefect, so one risky test would leave the gate scoring a near-empty
      # coverage report as if it had scored everything.
      - name: Generate coverage for mutation testing
        run: >-
          php -d memory_limit=1G vendor/bin/phpunit
          --testsuite=unit
          --no-extensions
          --do-not-fail-on-risky
          --coverage-xml build/infection-coverage/coverage-xml
          --log-junit build/infection-coverage/junit.xml

      # Size memory_limit for the reports rather than for the run: Infection holds
      # every mutant result and encodes all of them into build/infection.json once
      # the score is printed, so a large source tree exhausts a limit the scoring
      # itself never came close to.
      - name: Mutation testing on changed lines
        if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
        run: >-
          php -d memory_limit=4G vendor/bin/infection
          --configuration=infection.json5
          --threads=max
          --coverage=build/infection-coverage
          --skip-initial-tests
          --git-diff-lines
          --git-diff-base="origin/${GITHUB_BASE_REF}"
          --ignore-msi-with-no-mutations
          --min-msi=85
          --min-covered-msi=85
          --no-progress
          --logger-github

      - name: Mutation testing on the whole source tree
        if: github.event_name != 'pull_request'
        run: >-
          php -d memory_limit=4G vendor/bin/infection
          --configuration=infection.json5
          --threads=max
          --coverage=build/infection-coverage
          --skip-initial-tests
          --no-progress
          --logger-github
{
